title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Closeout Set: Rate-Hike Talk Wipes Out Morning Rally
conditions.summary: Stocks opened higher on Anthropic's debut but reversed hard as Fed rate-hike talk spread, with the Dow down about 1,100 points and the S&P 500 off 2% for a sixth straight loss.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: The S&P 500 fell 2.0% to 7,175.83, its sixth straight losing session.
The Dow dropped 1,101 points, or 2.2%, to 49,097.06; the Nasdaq lost 2.3% to 23,879.20; the Russell 2000 slid 1.8% to 2,664.79.
Stocks opened higher, with the S&P up about 1% early, before Fed rate-hike talk erased the gains by midday.
Selling hit nearly every sector; only energy and consumer staples finished slightly higher, while industrials fell about 2.6% and health care lagged.
The VIX jumped about 14% to near 28, around its highest level since March.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: Minutes from the Fed's October meeting showed nearly all officials favoring another rate hike soon, and some discussed a half-point move.
Futures pricing showed about a 90% chance of a quarter-point hike at the December 8-9 meeting.
Initial jobless claims rose to 203,000, above the 196,000 expected; continuing claims climbed to 1.763 million.
The Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index plunged to 6.3 from 20.9, far below forecasts near 20.

The 10-year Treasury yield eased about 1 basis point to roughly 5.05%; gold fell about 2% to near $3,665; WTI crude rose about 0.9% to around $83; bitcoin slipped to near $61,800; the dollar index was near 103.8, close to a 19-month high, in morning trade.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: ANT (Anthropic): +17.1% — priced its IPO at $83, opened at $111.50 and closed at $97.17 after raising about $81.3 billion.
INSM (Insmed): +20.6% — reports said Sanofi is considering an acquisition.
PANW (Palo Alto Networks): +6.4% — stronger-than-expected quarter, raised outlook and a $4.5 billion all-stock deal for Applied Compute.
PDD (PDD Holdings): +11.0% — rallied after third-quarter results.
AMD (Advanced Micro Devices): -7.7% — a report alleged a blacklisted Chinese server maker kept getting AMD firmware.
NVDA (Nvidia): -3.3% — chip and AI names gave back early gains.
AMZN (Amazon): -3.9% — fell along with other big tech stocks.
UNH (UnitedHealth): -3.2% — health insurers slid on a proposal to expand Medicare Advantage audits.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Walmart topped revenue estimates at $188.8 billion and raised its outlook, but the stock dipped about 1%.
Williams-Sonoma fell 15% after keeping its full-year outlook unchanged.
Valvoline rose 10% on a 22% sales jump; Liquidity Services fell about 25%.
StoneX sank about 27% after results released late Wednesday.
After the close, Intuit fell about 14.5% and Ross Stores about 9% in early after-hours trading; Gap also reported.

sections.title: Business News
items: Anthropic's debut was one of the largest IPOs on record, valuing the AI company at about $1.5 trillion at the offer price.
Intuit agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons.
Texas resumed its review of data center permits.
Vivid Seats jumped about 63% after a debt recapitalization that gives lenders roughly 80% of its stock.
JPMorgan said a cyberattack on a third-party vendor did not disrupt its services.

sections.title: On Deck
items: 9:00 AM CT: final University of Michigan consumer sentiment for November (forecast 51.0, prior 48.0).
Anthropic's IPO is expected to formally close.
Monthly options expiration could add volatility.
Markets keep watching Fed comments ahead of the December 8-9 meeting.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Thursday, November nineteenth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sliding into the water, the last set is rolling in, and folks, it was a gnarly one out there. Gus the wonder dog spent the afternoon guarding my sandals from the seagulls. Give the crew a good evening woof, Gus! Here's the final set. The Dow wiped out, down about eleven hundred points, or two point two percent, to forty-nine thousand ninety-seven. The S and P five hundred fell two percent to about seven thousand one hundred seventy-six. That's six losing days in a row. The Nasdaq dropped two and a quarter percent to about twenty-three thousand eight hundred seventy-nine. The Russell two thousand slid one point eight percent. And here's the kook move of the day. Stocks paddled out higher this morning, with the S and P up about one percent early. Then talk of more Fed rate hikes rolled in like a closeout set, and the gains washed away. Selling hit nearly every sector, and only energy and consumer staples stayed above water. Now for wind and weather. Fed minutes out last night showed nearly all policymakers leaning toward another hike soon. Traders now see about a ninety percent chance of a quarter point hike at the December meeting. Jobless claims rose to two hundred three thousand, above the one hundred ninety-six thousand expected. The Philly Fed factory index sank to six point three, far below forecasts. The ten year Treasury yield eased about one basis point to around five point oh five percent. The fear gauge, the VIX, jumped to about twenty-eight. Gold fell about two percent, while crude oil rose almost one percent. Let's check the lineup. The big story was the grommet that's already a giant. Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq today. It priced at eighty-three dollars, opened at one hundred eleven fifty, and closed at ninety-seven seventeen, up about seventeen percent. Insmed caught the biggest wave of the big names, up about twenty and a half percent on reports that Sanofi is eyeing a deal. Insmed rode that one all the way to the sand. Gus, that's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! Palo Alto Networks hung ten, up about six and a half percent on strong results and a four and a half billion dollar deal. On the wipeout side, A M D dropped almost eight percent after a report tied it to a blacklisted Chinese server maker. Nvidia fell three point three percent and Amazon nearly four. On the tide chart, Walmart beat on revenue and raised its outlook, but the stock slipped about one percent. Williams-Sonoma sank fifteen percent after holding its outlook steady. After the bell, Intuit fell about fourteen percent and Ross Stores about nine percent in late trading. Beach talk. Intuit agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons. Texas resumed its review of data center permits. Tomorrow's forecast. The final University of Michigan consumer sentiment reading lands at nine A M Central. Anthropic's stock sale is expected to officially close, and it's monthly options expiration, so expect some chop. Soul surfers, remember that six-day losing streaks come and go. Wax your board, rest up, and catch the Dawn Patrol in the morning. Got a stock, E T F or futures contract on your mind?
